artworks.title: The Shepherd Aristaeus Mourning the Loss of His Bees
artworks.description: Hiolle's Prix de Rome plaster: Aristaeus sunk beside an empty hive — Georgics IV's bee-loss that drives him to Cyrene and the bugonia.

artworks.title: The Shepherd Aristaeus Mourning the Loss of His Bees
artworks.description: Fesquet's seated grieving Aristaeus — the same Virgilian apiary disaster, second prize in the 1862 sculpture contest.

artworks.title: Cup with Eurydice, Aristaeus and Orpheus
artworks.description: Urbino maiolica: Aristaeus pursues Eurydice while Orpheus looks on — the chase that kills the nymph and dooms Aristaeus' bees.

artworks.title: Aristaeus, God of the Gardens
artworks.description: Bosio's Louvre marble: the rustic culture-god of bees, oil, and the chase — the husbandry hero whose cycle Virgil made Roman farming myth.

popCulture.title: Georgics
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Virgil's fourth Georgic retells Aristaeus' bees and the Orpheus digression — the culture-hero of husbandry as Roman poetry's farming myth.

popCulture.title: Aristaeus
popCulture.description: Aristaeus remains the rustic god of bees, oil and the chase — the cycle of loss and restoration that taught Greeks to keep hives.
